The CDP/PNRR standards supplied are grant-specific: they include net room and function areas per bed, accessible-bed provisions, and bathroom requirements, while no verified minimum gross property area is available. The property’s energy class E and energy score total of 8 indicate scope for energy improvement. Urban-planning compatibility, change-of-use authorization, building suitability, accessibility, fire and structural safety, and other required approvals need verification before determining grant eligibility.
pros: Strong proximity to education services (83.1), aligning with the stated preference.
Good access to commercial services (89.2) and public mobility (78.2), supporting resident convenience.
Existing office-building use provides a potential starting point for conversion, subject to layout and authorization checks.
cons: At 143.0 sqm, the property’s gross area does not establish whether grant-specific net room, function, accessible-bed, and bathroom standards can be met; no verified gross-area threshold is supplied.
Energy class E and energy score total 8 indicate relatively weak energy performance and likely improvement needs.
Turin PRG compatibility, change of use, hygiene, accessibility, fire and structural safety, and sector-specific approvals remain unverified.

evaluation_results.evaluation_text: The office building’s central Turin location and comparatively strong access to public transport, education, healthcare, green areas, and commercial services support its initial strategic appeal. However, the supplied 40.0 m² surface area alone cannot establish whether a student residence layout or required facilities can be accommodated. The cited CDP/PNRR standards are grant-specific and include net area requirements by bed and room, accessible beds, and bathroom area; there is no verified minimum gross property area threshold to apply here. Urban-planning compatibility, change-of-use authorization, hygiene, accessibility, fire safety where required, structural safety, and sector authorization all need verification. Its weak energy profile also signals likely retrofit needs.
pros: Office building in Turin, with proximity indicators showing strong public transport access (87.3) and comparatively strong access to education (66.4), healthcare (66.1), green areas (78.6), and commercial services (75.8).
The existing office use gives the property a potential conversion starting point, subject to verifying the permitted use, building layout, and required authorizations.

The provided 40.0 m² surface area is not, by itself, grounds to reject the property: the supplied grant-specific standards concern net area by function and bed, while no verified gross-area threshold is available.
cons: At 40.0 m², the documented area provides limited evidence of capacity; the data do not establish bed numbers, room configuration, accessible accommodation, or whether required net areas can be met.
The building’s energy class E and energy score total of 6 indicate a weak energy profile and potential retrofit requirements.
Compatibility with Turin’s planning rules and change of use, hygiene, accessibility, fire safety where required, structural and seismic safety, and sector authorization remain unverified.

evaluation_results.evaluation_text: This 156 sqm office building in Turin offers a plausible starting point for conversion to student housing, with strong commercial proximity, good public transport access, and an education proximity score of 65.4. These location indicators support the objective, although no specific gross-area, bed-capacity, energy, or transport threshold was requested. Its age and reported energy performance suggest that refurbishment may be needed. The supplied data do not establish room layout, accessibility, planning compatibility, change-of-use authorization, or technical feasibility, all of which require verification. The CDP/PNRR standard is specific to that funding program: it includes net residential-area requirements by bed and room, accessible-bed provisions, and bathroom-area criteria. The 156 sqm gross property area cannot establish compliance with those net standards, and no verified minimum gross-property threshold is provided.
pros: Office building type provides a potential conversion starting point for the student-residence objective, subject to planning and technical checks.
Strong commercial proximity (88.2) and good mobility proximity (76.6) support access to services and transport.
Education proximity (65.4) is consistent with the stated preference for nearby educational services.
cons: At 156 sqm gross, the property’s capacity and ability to meet the program’s net room and per-bed standards cannot be determined from the supplied data.
Planning compatibility, change-of-use authorization, accessibility, hygiene, fire, structural, seismic, and sector-specific requirements remain to be verified.
Energy class E and a total energy score of 10 indicate potential for energy improvement; the building dates from 1919–1945.
